Action Plan:
1. Urgent self-presentation to the hospital today for assessment of acute shortness of breath 4 weeks post–cesarean section to rule out venous thromboembolism (including pulmonary embolism). Patient declined ambulance and will take herself, bringing necessary items for the baby.
2. Avoid taking codeine until after hospital evaluation.
3. Pulse found to be slightly fast on self-check; to be reassessed in hospital.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: New-onset shortness of breath.
- History of presenting complaint:
  • Shortness of breath started about 1 hour prior to call, at rest while watching TV.  
  • Not known to be worsening.  
  • No chest pain reported; chest soreness with deep inspiration noted (patient also reports C-section scar tenderness).  
  • New cough since yesterday; non-productive.  
  • Sensation of heart “really going” (palpitations).
  • Postpartum status: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
  • Infant well with no respiratory symptoms.
  • Family history mentioned: mother has had leg clots.
- Past medical history: No other medical problems reported.
- Past surgical history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Medications:
  • Codeine for post-op pain; dose/route/frequency not documented. Used regularly initially; not taken for approximately 1 week. Advised to avoid currently.
- Social history:
  • At home with baby; partner at work. Patient plans to self-transport to hospital with baby.
- Allergies:
  • Ibuprofen — reaction not documented.

Objective:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals recorded.
- Patient-performed pulse count: 30 beats during a brief timed interval (exact duration not documented). Physician assessed heart rate as slightly fast.
- No other examination findings or investigations documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute shortness of breath 4 weeks postpartum:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism (suspected).
   - Investigations planned: Urgent hospital evaluation for possible venous thromboembolism (tests to be determined by hospital).
   - Treatment planned: Hospital management as indicated; clinician advised that treatment may be given to reduce a clot if confirmed (specific therapy not discussed).
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent self-presentation to hospital/emergency department today.

2. Palpitations/tachycardia:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Sinus tachycardia (suspected).
   - Investigations planned: To be assessed in hospital alongside evaluation for shortness of breath.
   - Treatment planned: Avoid codeine until after hospital assessment.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Full set of vitals; detailed review of systems; comprehensive past medical/surgical history; current medication list with doses/route/frequency; detailed ibuprofen allergy reaction; smoking status; obstetric/postpartum complications; breastfeeding status; safety-netting advice if deterioration prior to arrival not explicitly documented.
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially stated DOB as 04/20/1980; clinician then stated 1983 — conflict noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor pauses; clinically adequate history captured for urgent referral.
